name: Horizontal Row
definition: A strict compound horizontal pull whose concentric phase combines shoulder extension from a flexed start, scapular retraction, and elbow flexion while the torso and lower body resist rather than propel the load. The admitted upper-arm path remains tucked or within a modest scapular corridor. Wide or deliberately flared horizontal-abduction rows, the source-exact seated 45-degree cable pulldown, unreviewed commercial lever high rows, face pulls, momentum rows, renegade rows, and unreviewed bodyweight inclinations or apparatuses remain outside this contract. The measured 45-degree fixture routes to diagonal-pull; product-named lever high rows do not inherit that ownership without geometry review.

variantAxes.description: Whether the distal segment moves freely or remains fixed.
The torso and setup relationship during the row.
The lower-body contact that materially changes effective bodyweight loading; none when no such contact participates.
The external surface directly supporting the anterior torso during the row.
Whether external support limits scapular translation along the thorax; this does not classify rotation or tilt.
Canonical forearm and hand orientation through the working range.
Categorical bilateral hand spacing on the shared narrow-to-wide scale; absent for unilateral exercises.
Whether the upper arm remains tucked near the torso or travels through a modest scapular corridor without becoming flared.
Whether rails or a lever constrain the external load path; distal hand fixation remains kineticChain.
The machine mechanism when equipment is machine.
Whether a lever-row machine's left and right arms are mechanically linked or can move independently; absent for Smith rails and non-lever equipment.
Whether hip, knee, or ankle drive contributes to the concentric pull.
Whether the external load remains unsupported or resets on the floor between repetitions.
Whether the opposite hand and knee support the body without directly supporting the torso.
The fixed apparatus held during a bodyweight row.
The reviewed body geometry used to anchor effective bodyweight loading.

exerciseRules.description: Bodyweight rows use a closed chain, feet-supported suspended body, and explicit apparatus and leverage without pinning grip or upper-arm path.
The reviewed parallel feet-on-floor leverage pins body position, support, equipment, and the 0.73 effective-bodyweight anchor.
A straight fixed bar belongs to a bodyweight row and admits pronated or supinated rather than neutral grip.
Every externally loaded row is open chain, has no bodyweight leverage support, and uses zero bodyweight fraction.
Machine rows declare a constrained external path and their reviewed mechanism.
Non-machine rows use an unconstrained external-load path and omit machine mechanism metadata.
A lever row is a seated, machine-pad-supported machine using neutral or pronated grip without contralateral support.
A Smith row is a bilateral pronated hip-hinged machine row without torso or contralateral support.
A lever-row machine with mechanically linked left and right arms is authored only as a bilateral exercise.
A barbell row is an unsupported hip-hinged free-path pull using pronated or supinated grip.
Dumbbell rows use neutral grip and a free path in a hip-hinged or prone position.
A prone row is the bilateral chest-supported dumbbell branch.
A cable row is seated without torso support, uses neutral or pronated grip, and never resets between repetitions.
Bench torso support belongs only to a bilateral prone dumbbell row.
Machine-pad torso support belongs to a seated lever-row machine.
Hand-and-knee contralateral support belongs to an unsupported unilateral hip-hinged dumbbell row.
Bilateral rows do not declare one-sided hand-and-knee support.
A bilateral row declares categorical hand spacing.
A unilateral row is limited to dumbbell, cable, or machine equipment, omits bilateral width, and declares pelvic and oblique control.
Hip-hinged rows declare spinal, pelvic, and hip stability with lower-back and gluteal stabilizers.
A suspended inverted row declares spinal, pelvic, and hip stability with abdominal, lower-back, and gluteal stabilizers.
A row without direct torso support declares spinal stability and at least one reviewed trunk stabilizer.
A floor-reset row is a strict bilateral pronated barbell row in an unsupported hip hinge without lower-body drive.
A narrow bilateral grip remains in the tucked shoulder-extension corridor.
A supinated grip remains in the tucked shoulder-extension corridor.

execution.startingPosition: Stand holding a barbell at shoulder width with your palms facing back. Hinge at your hips until your torso is inclined.
execution.movement: Pull the bar toward your lower ribs while your elbows travel back near your torso.
execution.endpoint: End the pull with the bar at your lower ribs.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep your hips and knees still while only your arms pull.
execution.supportAndPosture: Brace your trunk without changing the torso angle.
disqualifyingCompensations: Standing up during the pull turns the bent-over row into an upright row.
Resetting the bar on the floor between repetitions turns the continuous row into a dead-stop row.
Jerking the bar with the lower back turns the strict row into a momentum row.

execution.startingPosition: Hold a barbell at shoulder width with your palms facing forward.
execution.movement: Pull the bar toward your lower torso.
execution.endpoint: End the pull with the bar at your lower torso.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep your elbows tucked and do not stand up during the pull.
execution.supportAndPosture: Maintain a strict hip hinge with your trunk braced.
disqualifyingCompensations: Turning the palms away from facing forward turns the underhand row into an overhand row.
Standing up to heave the bar turns the strict hinged row into a momentum row.

execution.startingPosition: Set a barbell on the floor and hold it at shoulder width with your palms facing back.
execution.movement: Pull the bar toward your lower ribs.
execution.endpoint: End the pull with the bar at your lower ribs.
execution.returnPhase: Lower the bar to a complete floor reset. Rebrace before the next repetition.
execution.controlledJoints: Do not stand up or arch your back during the pull.
execution.supportAndPosture: Bend forward from your hips and brace your trunk.
disqualifyingCompensations: Keeping the bar floating between repetitions turns the Pendlay row into a continuous bent-over row.
Bouncing the bar off the floor turns the dead-stop reset into a momentum row.

execution.startingPosition: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing inward. Establish a strict hip hinge.
execution.movement: Pull both dumbbells toward the sides of your lower torso.
execution.endpoint: End the pull with the dumbbells beside your lower torso.
execution.returnPhase: Lower the dumbbells without changing your trunk angle.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep your elbows close during the pull.
disqualifyingCompensations: Rowing one dumbbell at a time turns the two-arm row into a one-arm row.
Standing up to swing the dumbbells turns the strict row into a momentum row.

execution.startingPosition: Place your opposite hand and knee on a bench while the foot on your working side stays planted. Hold one dumbbell with your palm facing inward.
execution.movement: Pull your working elbow toward your hip.
execution.endpoint: End the pull with the dumbbell beside your hip.
execution.controlledJoints: Do not rotate your torso during the pull.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep your hips level and facing forward.
disqualifyingCompensations: Twisting the torso to swing the dumbbell turns the strict one-arm row into a momentum row.
Lifting the supporting hand or knee off the bench turns the supported row into an unsupported hinge row.
execution.sideOrDirection: Complete all repetitions on one side, then switch to the other arm.

execution.startingPosition: Lie face down with your chest supported on an incline bench and hold two dumbbells with your palms facing inward.
execution.movement: Pull your elbows toward your lower torso, letting your shoulder blades move around your rib cage.
execution.endpoint: End the pull with your elbows beside your lower torso.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep your legs and lower body still while your arms pull.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep your chest supported on the incline bench.
disqualifyingCompensations: Lifting the chest off the bench to heave the dumbbells turns the supported row into a momentum row.
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears turns the row into a shrug.

execution.startingPosition: Sit upright at a low cable station holding a narrow parallel handle with your palms facing each other.
execution.movement: Pull the handle toward your lower ribs.
execution.endpoint: End the pull with the handle at your lower ribs.
execution.returnPhase: Return the handle until your shoulder blades move forward under control.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep your torso steady without back support.
disqualifyingCompensations: Leaning back to swing the handle turns the strict seated row into a momentum row.
Rocking the torso back and forth turns the seated row into a rowing-machine stroke.

execution.startingPosition: Sit upright at a low cable station and hold one handle with your palm facing inward.
execution.movement: Pull your working elbow toward your hip.
execution.endpoint: End the pull with your working elbow beside your hip.
execution.returnPhase: Return your arm forward without rotating your torso.
execution.controlledJoints: Do not rotate your torso during the pull or the return.
execution.supportAndPosture: Brace your trunk and keep your pelvis square.
disqualifyingCompensations: Twisting the torso to drag the handle turns the one-arm row into a rotational pull.
Leaning away from the cable to move the weight turns the strict row into a momentum row.
execution.sideOrDirection: Complete all repetitions on one side, then switch to the other arm.

execution.startingPosition: Sit at a linked-arm row machine with your chest against the pad and hold the handles with your palms facing each other.
execution.movement: Let your shoulder blades move naturally as you drive your elbows toward your lower ribs.
execution.endpoint: End the pull with your elbows beside your lower ribs.
execution.returnPhase: Return the linked lever under control.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep your legs and torso still while the lever moves.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep your chest against the pad.
disqualifyingCompensations: Lifting the chest off the pad turns the supported machine row into an unsupported pull.
Pushing with the legs turns the strict machine row into a leg-assisted pull.

execution.startingPosition: Sit against the chest pad of a single-arm row machine and hold one handle with your palm facing inward.
execution.movement: Pull your working elbow toward your lower torso.
execution.endpoint: End the pull with your working elbow beside your lower torso.
execution.returnPhase: Return the lever without twisting away from the pad.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep your free arm and legs still while one arm pulls.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep your pelvis and chest square.
disqualifyingCompensations: Twisting away from the pad turns the supported one-arm row into a rotational pull.
Lifting the chest off the pad turns the machine row into an unsupported pull.
execution.sideOrDirection: Complete all repetitions on one side, then switch to the other arm.

execution.startingPosition: Set the Smith bar near knee height and hold it at shoulder width with your palms facing back.
execution.movement: Pull the bar toward your lower ribs.
execution.endpoint: End the pull with the bar at your lower ribs.
execution.returnPhase: Lower the bar along the rails under control.
execution.controlledJoints: Do not change your torso angle during the pull.
execution.supportAndPosture: Establish a strict hip hinge beneath the rail path.
disqualifyingCompensations: Standing up during the pull turns the hinged Smith row into an upright pull.
Bouncing the bar between repetitions turns the strict row into a momentum row.

execution.startingPosition: Lie beneath a fixed straight bar, hold it at shoulder width with your palms facing away from you, and keep your feet on the floor with your body nearly parallel to it.
execution.movement: Pull your chest toward the bar while letting your shoulder blades move naturally.
execution.endpoint: End the pull with your chest at the bar.
execution.controlledJoints: Do not bend at the hips or knees during the pull.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep a straight line from your shoulders through your heels.
disqualifyingCompensations: Bending at the hips turns the straight-body row into a bent-hip hang.
Kicking with the legs turns the strict row into a momentum row.
